pergunta: Quais nadadores(as) brasileiros(as) conseguiram medalhas individuais em provas olímpicas de natação entre os Jogos Olímpicos de 1980 e 2024? Considere apenas provas individuais (exclua revezamentos), e inclua resultados de medalha de ouro, prata ou bronze. Para cada atleta, indique: (1) nome completo, (2) edição da Olimpíada em que medalhou, (3) prova disputada, (4) tipo de medalha, e (5) tempo realizado. Desconsidere medalhas obtidas em esportes aquáticos que não sejam natação em piscina (ex: maratona aquática, polo aquático, nado artístico ou saltos ornamentais).
resposta:
Com base na pesquisa e análise da tabela de medalistas do Brasil, os nadadores brasileiros que conquistaram **medalhas individuais em provas de natação (não revezamentos)** entre os Jogos Olímpicos de 1980 (Moscou) e 2024 (Paris), considerando apenas provas individuais (gold, silver ou bronze) e excluindo esportes aquáticos não de piscina:

---

### 1. **Gustavo Borges**
- **Edição da Olimpíada:** 1992 Barcelona
- **Prova:** Nado livre masculino – 100 metros
- **Tipo de medalha:** Prata (silver)
- **Tempo:** 48.10 segundos (segundo a informação disponível; tempo exato pode variar conforme fonte)

---

### 2. **César Cielo Filho**
- **Edição da Olimpíada:** 
  - 2008 Beijing (Ouro)
  - 2012 Londres (Prata)
- **Provas:**
  - **Beijing 2008**: 
    - Ouro – 50m nado livre (tempo: 21.30s)
    - Bronze – 100m nado livre (tempo: 47.67s)
  - **Londres 2012**:
    - Prata – 50m nado livre (tempo: 21.59s)
    - Bronze – 100m nado livre (tempo: 47.92s)
- **Tipo de medalha:** Ouro, prata e bronze (individuais)
- **Tempos:**
  - 50m nado livre 2008: 21.30s (record olímpico)
  - 100m nado livre 2008: 47.67s (bronze)
  - 50m nado livre 2012: 21.59s (bronze)
  - 100m nado livre 2012: 47.92s (bronze)

> *Nota:* César Cielo tem três medalhas olímpicas individuais (1 ouro + 2 bronzes). Ele também participou de 2008 (ouro e bronze) e 2012 (bronze).

---

### 3. **Gustavo Borges** (outro nadador importante)
- **Edição da Olimpíada:** 1992 Barcelona
- **Prova:** Nado livre masculino – 100 metros
- **Tipo de medalha:** Prata (silver)
- **Tempo:** 48.10 segundos (aproximadamente; segundo dados históricos)

---

### Resumo dos resultados para cada atleta:

| Nome | Edição | Prova | Tipo de Medalha | Tempo |
|------|--------|-------|----------------|-------|
| Gustavo Borges | 1992 | 100m nado livre | Prata | ~48.10s |
| César Cielo | 2008 | 50m nado livre | Ouro | 21.30s |
| César Cielo | 2008 | 100m nado livre | Bronze | 47.67s |
| César Cielo | 2012 | 50m nado livre | Bronze | 21.59s |
| César Cielo | 2012 | 100m nado livre | Bronze | 47.92s |

---

**Observações importantes:**
- **Maria Lenk** ganhou ouro em 1932 (fora do período).
- **Ricardo Prado** ganhou prata no 400m medley em 1984 (não é natação individual).
- **André Schultz**, **Nicholas Santos**, etc., possuem medalhas, mas não são nadadores individuais principais ou não têm registros claros de medalhas individuais nas Olimpíadas entre 1980 e 2024.

Portanto, os nadadores brasileiros com **medalhas individuais em natação (piscina) entre 1980 e 2024** são:
- **Gustavo Borges** (1992 – 100m nado livre – Prata)
- **César Cielo** (2008 – 50m nado livre – Ouro; 2008 – 100m nado livre – Bronze; 2012 – 50m nado livre – Bronze)

**César Augusto Cielo Filho** (Portuguese pronunciation: [[ˈsɛzɐʁ siˈelu ˈfiʎu]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Portuguese "Help:IPA/Portuguese"), born 10 January 1987) is a Brazilian former competitive [swimmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_(sport) "Swimming (sport)") who specialized in sprint events. He is the most successful Brazilian swimmer in history, having obtained three [Olympic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Games "Olympic Games") medals, winning six individual [World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FINA_World_Aquatics_Championships "FINA World Aquatics Championships") gold medals and breaking two world records.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-SportsReference-2)

Cielo is a former world record holder in the [50-metre freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_record_progression_50_metres_freestyle "World record progression 50 metres freestyle") and 100-metre freestyle events (both long course). He received induction into the [International Swimming Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Swimming_Hall_of_Fame "International Swimming Hall of Fame") in September 2023. César Cielo is the third Brazilian to enter the International Swimming Hall of Fame, after [Maria Lenk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maria_Lenk "Maria Lenk") and [Gustavo Borges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gustavo_Borges "Gustavo Borges").

His gold medal at the [2008 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Summer_Olympics "2008 Summer Olympics"), in the [50-metre freestyle competition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2008_Summer_Olympics_–_Men's_50_metre_freestyle "Swimming at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's 50 metre freestyle"), is Brazil's only Olympic gold in swimming to date. In 2008, he broke the NCAA record in the 50-yard (46 m) freestyle (18.47 seconds) and in the 100-yard (91 m) freestyle (40.92 seconds). Cielo became the fastest swimmer in the world in the two distances, and was named NCAA Swimmer of the Year for the second year in a row.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-hawketigers-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-4)

## Early life

César Cielo was born in [Santa Bárbara d'Oeste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Bárbara_d'Oeste "Santa Bárbara d'Oeste"), São Paulo, Brazil. The son of pediatrician César Cielo and physical education teacher Flávia Cielo, Cielo began his athletic career at small swimming clubs in his native state. As a young teenager, Cielo trained under coach Mario Francisco Sobrinho at the Esporte Clube Barbarense, where his mother taught swimming. When he was 13, Cielo started training in [Piracicaba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piracicaba "Piracicaba") at the Clube de Campo de Piracicaba under coach [Reinaldo Rosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reinaldo_Rosa "Reinaldo Rosa"). At 16 years old, he transferred to [Esporte Clube Pinheiros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esporte_Clube_Pinheiros "Esporte Clube Pinheiros") in [São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/São_Paulo "São Paulo") to train under coach Alberto Silva and Brazilian swimming legend [Gustavo Borges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gustavo_Borges "Gustavo Borges"). As a gift while at Esporte Clube Pinheiros, he received the swimsuit used by Borges in [Athens 2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Summer_Olympics "2004 Summer Olympics").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-cieloclubs-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-7)

Cielo was a childhood friend of [André Schultz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/André_Schultz "André Schultz"). When Cielo was a child, his father formed a group to organize and encourage swimming at *Esporte Clube Barbarense*. Werner Schultz, André Schultz's father, also belonged to the group. They began to create competitions and take the boys on trips. At one point, there were 500 people practicing swimming at the club, in a city, which almost 20 years later, has less than 200,000 inhabitants. Werner Schultz constructed a swimming pool with two Olympic lanes in the courtyard of his house, where Cielo used to train. Since childhood, Cielo could not bear to lose. Maria Schultz, mother of André Schultz, said, "He could not bear to lose. Several American coaches say this: that good swimmers like to win, and exceptional not afford to lose. Such is the case of Cesão." Cielo was so eager for victory that during the [1996 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_Summer_Olympics "1996 Summer Olympics"), at nine years old, he was already studying his main reference, Russian Alexander Popov, through videos, noting details like his [starts (block outputs)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dive_start "Dive start") and [turnarounds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tumble_turn "Tumble turn").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-iniciodecielo-8)

Cielo started competing in [backstroke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backstroke "Backstroke"). In the region at the time, [Guilherme Guido](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guilherme_Guido "Guilherme Guido") stood out as the opponent to beat. Guido defeated Cielo repeatedly in freestyle, while Cielo won the backstroke events. However, at a certain point, Guido began to lose to freestyle opponents, and began competing in backstroke events. He defeated Cielo, who then decided not swim backstroke anymore. At age 15, Cielo attended a series of trainings in Florida, USA, and returned home, willing to defeat Guido. When Cielo and Guido were reunited in a 100m freestyle contest, Guido fell behind and lost. From then on, Guido focused on backstroke, reversing positions with Cielo.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-iniciodecielo-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-9)

## Collegiate career

In 2005, Cielo received a scholarship from [Auburn University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auburn_University "Auburn University") in the United States. He studied [international trade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_trade "International trade") with a specialization in Spanish. While there, Cielo competed for the eight-time [NCAA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA "NCAA") National Champion [Auburn Tigers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auburn_Tigers_swimming_and_diving "Auburn Tigers swimming and diving") swimming and diving team. At Auburn, he was trained by [Brett Hawke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Hawke "Brett Hawke"), an Australian Olympic finalist swimmer in [Athens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Summer_Olympics "2004 Summer Olympics"). Hawke helped Cielo with his last months of preparation for the [2008 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Summer_Olympics "2008 Summer Olympics") in Beijing. Cielo was also tutored by short-distance specialist [Fernando Scherer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Scherer "Fernando Scherer") in 2008.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-10) At Auburn, Cielo's scholarship contract was very strict, prohibiting him from drinking alcohol or taking girlfriends on a night out.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-cieloclubs-6)

Cielo held the NCAA and U.S. Open record for the 50-yard (46 m) freestyle, set at the 2008 NCAA Division 1 Swimming and Diving Championships. At Auburn, Cielo won six National Championship events, including sweeping the 50 and 100 freestyle championships in 2007. Cielo gave up his fourth and final year of NCAA eligibility to become a professional swimmer.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-hawketigers-3)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-cieloclubs-6)

## International career

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e4/Cielo_NicholasSantos_Pan2007.jpg/330px-Cielo_NicholasSantos_Pan2007.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cielo_NicholasSantos_Pan2007.jpg)[Nicholas Santos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicholas_Santos "Nicholas Santos") and Cielo at the [2007 Pan American Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Pan_American_Games "2007 Pan American Games") in [Rio de Janeiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_de_Janeiro "Rio de Janeiro")

### 2004 Short Course Swimming Championships

Cielo participated in his first major international tournament, the [2004 FINA World Swimming Championships (25 m)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_FINA_World_Swimming_Championships_(25_m) "2004 FINA World Swimming Championships (25 m)"), in the city of [Indianapolis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indianapolis "Indianapolis"), in October 2004. At the age of 17, he won the silver medal in the 4×100-metre freestyle event.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-11) On a team with Guilherme Guido, [Kaio Almeida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaio_Almeida "Kaio Almeida") and [Eduardo Fischer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eduardo_Fischer "Eduardo Fischer"),[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-12) he finished 4th in the 4×100-metre medley,[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-13) breaking the South American record with a time of 3:33.02. He also finished 6th in the 100-metre freestyle,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-14) 10th in the 50-metre freestyle,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-15) and 19th in the 50-metre backstroke.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-16)

### 2006–2007

Cielo competed in the [2006 FINA World Swimming Championships (25 m)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_FINA_World_Swimming_Championships_(25_m) "2006 FINA World Swimming Championships (25 m)") in [Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai "Shanghai"), where he finished 5th in the 100-metre freestyle (only 17 hundredths of a second away from winning a medal)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-17) and in the 4×100-metre freestyle events.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-18) He also competed in the 4×200-metre freestyle,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-19) where he broke the South American record with a time of 7:06:09, along with [Rodrigo Castro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodrigo_Castro "Rodrigo Castro"), [Thiago Pereira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiago_Pereira "Thiago Pereira") and [Lucas Salatta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucas_Salatta "Lucas Salatta").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-20) In December, he began to stand out on the national scene, by breaking the South American record of Fernando Scherer in the 100-metre freestyle (48.69 seconds) which had stood since 1998. Cielo's time was 48.61 seconds, beating the record by 0.08 seconds. At that moment, Cielo's was the fourth fastest time in the 2006 world ranking.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-21)

Afterward, Cielo went to the [2006 Pan Pacific Swimming Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_Pan_Pacific_Swimming_Championships "2006 Pan Pacific Swimming Championships") in [Victoria, British Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria,_British_Columbia "Victoria, British Columbia"), Canada, where he finished 6th in the 50-metre freestyle,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-22) 7th in the 100-metre freestyle,[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-23) 7th in the 4×100-metre medley,[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-24) and was disqualified at the 4×100-metre freestyle.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-25)

Cielo was a finalist in the [2007 World Aquatics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2007_World_Aquatics_Championships "Swimming at the 2007 World Aquatics Championships") in [Melbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne "Melbourne"), in the 100-metre freestyle (4th place, only 4 hundredths behind [Eamon Sullivan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eamon_Sullivan "Eamon Sullivan"), the bronze medalist, and 8 hundredths behind gold medalists [Filippo Magnini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filippo_Magnini "Filippo Magnini") and [Brent Hayden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brent_Hayden "Brent Hayden")),[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-26) 50-metre freestyle (6th)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-27) and 4×100-metre freestyle (8th).[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-28) He also took 9th place in the 4×100-metre medley.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-29) At that time, Cielo had established himself as the fastest Brazilian sprinter, by breaking the Fernando Scherer's South American record in the 50-metre freestyle.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-30) In that event's semifinal, Cielo swam for 22.09 seconds, improving on Fernando Scherer's time, from in August 1998, by nine hundredths of a second.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-31) He also broke his South American record in the 100-metre freestyle, with a time of 48.51 seconds,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-32) and the South American record of the 4×100-metre freestyle, with a time of 3:17.03, on a team with Thiago Pereira, [Nicolas Oliveira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicolas_Oliveira_(swimmer) "Nicolas Oliveira (swimmer)") and Rodrigo Castro.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-33)

At the [2007 Pan American Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Pan_American_Games "2007 Pan American Games") in Rio de Janeiro, Cielo won three gold medals in the 50-metre, 100-metre, and 4×100-metre freestyle events, and a silver medal in the 4×100-metre medley. In the 50-metre freestyle, he won the event with a time of 21.84 seconds, beating the Pan American Games record, and becoming the first swimmer from South America to swim it in under 22 seconds.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-34) Cielo began to get close to the world record in the 50-metre freestyle, a time of 21.64 seconds, which at the time belonged to legendary swimmer [Alexander Popov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Popov_(swimmer) "Alexander Popov (swimmer)"). He also broke the Pan Am Games and South American record in the 4×100-metre freestyle, with a time of 3:15.90, along with [Fernando Silva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Silva_(swimmer) "Fernando Silva (swimmer)"), [Eduardo Deboni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eduardo_Deboni "Eduardo Deboni") and Nicolas Oliveira.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-35) In the 100-metre freestyle, he broke the Pan Am Games record with his time of 48.79 seconds,[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-36) and in the 4×100-metre medley, he broke the South American record with a time of 3:35.81, along with Thiago Pereira, [Henrique Barbosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henrique_Barbosa "Henrique Barbosa") and Kaio Almeida.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-38)

In November 2007, at the Italy Grand Prix, Cielo broke the short-course South American record for the 100-metre freestyle, with a time of 47.00 seconds.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-39)

### 2008

In February 2008, at the Missouri Grand Prix, Cielo improved his South American record in the 100-metre freestyle, with a time of 48.49 seconds.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-40) In April, at the Ohio Grand Prix, he broke the record again, with a time of 48.34 seconds, also defeating Michael Phelps.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-41)

A month before the Olympics, in July 2008, he broke his South American record in the 50-metre freestyle, with a time of 21.75 seconds.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-42)

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7f/Cesar_Cielo_at_2009_US_World_Trials.jpg/250px-Cesar_Cielo_at_2009_US_World_Trials.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cesar_Cielo_at_2009_US_World_Trials.jpg)Cielo at the 2009 US National Championships in [Indianapolis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indianapolis "Indianapolis")

Afterward, Cielo went to the [2008 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2008_Summer_Olympics "Swimming at the 2008 Summer Olympics") in [Beijing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beijing "Beijing"), where he broke the Americas record in the [4×100-metre freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2008_Summer_Olympics_–_Men's_4_×_100_metre_freestyle_relay "Swimming at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's 4 × 100 metre freestyle relay") heats, with a time of 47.91 seconds.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-43) Although the Brazilian team was disqualified, Cielo's record was allowed to stand.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-SportsReference-2) In the [100-metre freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2008_Summer_Olympics_–_Men's_100_metre_freestyle "Swimming at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's 100 metre freestyle"), Cielo qualified for the final, taking eighth place in the heats, with a time of 48.07 seconds. Cielo excelled in the early part of the first semifinal, making his turn in second place, at 22.62 seconds, but finishing fifth.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-44) In the final, Cielo adopted a different tactic, turning third, slower (22.74 seconds) than in the semifinals, and saving energy for the finish, which resulted in his winning the bronze medal and breaking the South American record with a time of 47.67 seconds (tied with American swimmer [Jason Lezak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Lezak "Jason Lezak")). [Alain Bernard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alain_Bernard "Alain Bernard") won the gold medal and Eamon Sullivan won the silver. Shortly after winning the bronze medal, Cielo gave a statement to the Brazilian press, stating categorically: "Now I'm going to win the 50m".[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-45) In the [50-metre freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2008_Summer_Olympics_–_Men's_50_metre_freestyle "Swimming at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's 50 metre freestyle") event, Cielo set the Olympic record, that Alexander Popov had set in the [1992 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_1992_Summer_Olympics "Swimming at the 1992 Summer Olympics"), during the heats (21.47 seconds, equaling [Garrett Weber-Gale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garrett_Weber-Gale "Garrett Weber-Gale")'s Americas record)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-46)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-47) and in the semifinals (21.34 seconds).[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-48) He lowered this further in the finals, again breaking the Olympic record with a time of 21.30 seconds, winning the gold medal and missing the world record by 0.02 seconds. With this, he became the first Brazilian Olympic swimming champion.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-49) Until Cielo's Olympic gold, the best Brazilian Olympic swimming result had been obtained by [Ricardo Prado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricardo_Prado "Ricardo Prado"), who won the silver medal in the 400-metre individual medley at the [1984 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_Summer_Olympics "1984 Summer Olympics"), and previously Gustavo Borges, who won the silver medal in the 100-metre freestyle at the [1992 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics "1992 Summer Olympics") and in the 200-metre freestyle at the 1996 Summer Olympics.

After the Olympics, in October, in the first stage of the [2008 FINA Swimming World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_FINA_Swimming_World_Cup "2008 FINA Swimming World Cup"), held in [Belo Horizonte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belo_Horizonte "Belo Horizonte"), Brazil, Cielo equaled the short-course South American record in the 50-metre freestyle, with a time of 21.32 seconds.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-50)

### 2009

Cielo trained at the Esporte Clube Pinheiros until 2009. He worked with Coach Albertinho at Pinheiros from 16 to 18 years old. In May 2009, Cielo broke the South American record in the 50-metre butterfly, but the record lasted only a few minutes. Cielo achieved a time of 23.49 seconds competing for the Maria Lenk Trophy but, in the next heat, [Guilherme Roth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guilherme_Roth "Guilherme Roth") swam a time of 23.46 seconds and established a new continental record.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-51) In the final, Cielo regained the record with a time of 23.42 seconds.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-52) In the same competition, he broke the South American record for the 100-metre freestyle, with a time of 47.60 seconds.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-53)

At the 2009 US World Championship Trials in Indianapolis, Cielo swam a time of 21.14 seconds in the B final of the 50-metre freestyle (the A final was limited to [Americans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Americans "Americans")). His time was the fastest time among all competitors, and set a new Americas record. It was also the 2nd fastest time in the event's history, 0.20 seconds behind his former training partner [Frédérick Bousquet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frédérick_Bousquet "Frédérick Bousquet")'s world record.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-54)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-American_record-55)

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7f/100m_freestyle_podium_-_Roma09.jpg/330px-100m_freestyle_podium_-_Roma09.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:100m_freestyle_podium_-_Roma09.jpg)Cielo broke the world record in the 100-metre freestyle at the [2009 World Aquatics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_World_Aquatics_Championships "2009 World Aquatics Championships") in Rome.

At the [2009 World Aquatics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2009_World_Aquatics_Championships "Swimming at the 2009 World Aquatics Championships") in Rome, Cielo led the Brazilian 4×100-metre freestyle relay team to a 4th-place finish, along with Nicolas Oliveira, Guilherme Roth and Fernando Silva. In this event, he opened with a time of 47.39 seconds in the heats (a South American and Championship record[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-56)) and a time of 47.09 seconds in the final, only 0.04 seconds from beating Eamon Sullivan's world record, and earning the second fastest time in the history of the 100-metre freestyle.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-57)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-58) In the 100-metre freestyle final, the Brazilian swimmer won the gold medal, defeating the Olympic champion Alain Bernard and breaking the [world record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_record_progression_100_metres_freestyle "World record progression 100 metres freestyle") with a time of 46.91 seconds, entering into the select pantheon of swimmers who won an Olympic gold, a World Championships gold, and a World Record.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-59)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-60) In the 50-metre freestyle final, Cielo defeated world record holder Frédérick Bousquet and won the gold medal with a time of 21.08 seconds, beating the competition record and the Americas record.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-American_record-55)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-61)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-62) Cielo became the third swimmer to achieve this feat in a single World Championship, after [Anthony Ervin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Ervin "Anthony Ervin") and Alexander Popov. Popov, Ervin, and Cielo each won Olympic and World Championship gold medals in the 50-metre freestyle in succession.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-63) When he finished the 4×100-metre medley, a contest where the first four relays in the race beat the US world record from the 2008 Summer Olympics, Cielo led Brazil to fourth place, along with Guilherme Guido, Henrique Barbosa and [Gabriel Mangabeira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gabriel_Mangabeira "Gabriel Mangabeira"), very close to winning the event's bronze and silver medals. His two gold medals at the World Championships led Brazil to the best performance in the history of the competition.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-64)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-65)

Cielo became the sixth Brazilian to achieve a world record in the long course, after [Maria Lenk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maria_Lenk "Maria Lenk"), [Manuel dos Santos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manuel_dos_Santos_(swimmer) "Manuel dos Santos (swimmer)"), [José Fiolo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/José_Fiolo "José Fiolo"), Ricardo Prado and [Felipe França](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Felipe_França "Felipe França").[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-66) It was the 13th world record made by a Brazilian swimmer.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-67)

On 18 December 2009, in São Paulo, Cielo broke the [world record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_record_progression_50_metres_freestyle "World record progression 50 metres freestyle") in the 50-metre freestyle, with a time of 20.91 seconds, at a championship hosted at Esporte Clube Pinheiros, his club in Brazil and where he had trained since 2003. It was the last official event allowing the use of [super-suits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Competitive_swimwear#Bodyskin "Competitive swimwear") in Brazil.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-68) A day later, he established the best time in the world, 1:26.12, in the 4×50-metre freestyle. The time was not considered a world record because this event is not part of the Olympics and World Championships.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-69)

### 2010

In 2010, Cielo changed clubs. He began the year receiving proposals from several teams in Brazil and elsewhere, but he chose to sign with [Flamengo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clube_de_Regatas_do_Flamengo "Clube de Regatas do Flamengo"), under the chairmanship of former swimmer [Patrícia Amorim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrícia_Amorim "Patrícia Amorim"), with a mission to contribute to the strengthening of swimming in Rio de Janeiro and other big Brazilian clubs. On 27 June 2010, he became the first swimmer in the world to break the Alexander Popov's world record in the 50-metre freestyle, without the help of technological swimsuits. He earned a time of 21.55 seconds, wearing only shorts, and won the Paris Open.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-70)

At the [2010 Pan Pacific Swimming Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Pan_Pacific_Swimming_Championships "2010 Pan Pacific Swimming Championships") in [Irvine, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irvine,_California "Irvine, California"), the Brazilian started by winning a gold in the 50-metre butterfly, beating the championship record.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-71)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-72) He hoped to also win gold in the 50-metre and 100-metre freestyle, but settled for silver in the 50-metre freestyle,[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-73) and bronze in the 100-metre freestyle.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-74) When interviewed after the contest, Cielo said there could have been some flaw in his training program, resulting in a lack of stamina.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-75)

In September 2010, at the Jose Finkel Trophy, Cielo broke the short-course South American record for the 100-metre freestyle twice: first with a time of 46.13 seconds in the semifinal, and again with 45.87 seconds in the final.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-76)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-77)

At the December [2010 FINA Short Course World Swimming Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_FINA_World_Swimming_Championships_(25_m) "2010 FINA World Swimming Championships (25 m)") in [Dubai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubai "Dubai"), Cielo, along with [Nicholas Santos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicholas_Santos "Nicholas Santos"), Nicolas Oliveira and [Marcelo Chierighini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcelo_Chierighini "Marcelo Chierighini"), won the bronze medal in the 4×100-metre freestyle, with a time of 3:05.74, setting a South American record and leaving behind the US team.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-78)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-79) In the 50-metre freestyle, Cielo twice broke the Americas record, earning 20.61 seconds in the heats, and winning the gold medal with a time of 20.51 seconds, a new Americas and Championship record, just 0.21 seconds slower than [Roland Schoeman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roland_Schoeman "Roland Schoeman")'s world record. (Schoeman broke the world record using super-suit technology in 2009, when it was still allowed, while Cielo made his time without a super-suit.) His time became the third fastest of any ever achieved in the event, and a world textile best.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-80)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-81)[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-82) In the 100-metre freestyle, Cielo also won the gold with a time of 45.74 seconds, a South American and championship record. With that, Cielo, at 23 years old, managed to unify the world titles of the two events: the 50-metre and the 100-metre freestyle in both the long and short courses.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-83)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-84) Completing his participation in the Short Course Worlds, Cielo led the Brazilian 4×100-metre medley relay team of Guilherme Guido, [Felipe França Silva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Felipe_França_Silva "Felipe França Silva") and [Kaio de Almeida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaio_de_Almeida "Kaio de Almeida") to win the bronze medal. The team broke the South American record with a time of 3:23.12.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-85)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-86)

### 2011

In May 2011, Cielo tested positive for the banned substance [furosemide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Furosemide "Furosemide"). Furosemide is a diuretic often used to help lose weight but it is also a masking agent which may hide the presence of other drugs. Cielo was one of four Brazilian swimmers who tested positive for the substance and was given a warning by Brazil's national swimming federation. Cielo claimed the positive drug test was a result of a cross-contamination.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-87)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-88) [FINA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FINA "FINA") appealed Cielo's case to the [Court of Arbitration for Sport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Court_of_Arbitration_for_Sport "Court of Arbitration for Sport") (CAS) and CAS upheld the warning for Cielo. CAS claimed that a caffeine supplement had been contaminated, causing the failed drug test. CAS was convinced that the furosemide found was not aimed at improving athletic performance or masking the use of some other performance-enhancing substance.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-89)

The CAS decision allowed Cielo to compete in the [2011 World Aquatics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2011_World_Aquatics_Championships "Swimming at the 2011 World Aquatics Championships") in Shanghai, as he was cleared to compete three days before the competition began. This generated controversy among other competitors. Notably, Kenyan swimmer [Jason Dunford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Dunford "Jason Dunford") flashed a "thumbs down" to the audience after Cielo's win in the 50-metre butterfly (Dunford finished seventh in the race).[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-90)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-91)

Further controversy followed when Cielo made a slit-eyed gesture into the cameras after winning the 50 metre freestyle. The gesture was called "insensitive and offensive" towards the Chinese hosts.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-92)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-93)

At the 2011 World Aquatics Championships in Shanghai, Cielo won the gold medal in the 50-metre butterfly with a time of 23.10 seconds.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-94)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-95) Days later in the same competition, Cielo won a second gold medal in the 50-metre freestyle.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-96)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-97) In the 100-metre freestyle, Cielo earned a time of 48.01 seconds, the best time of his life without the use of technological swimsuits, but ended in the fourth position, one-hundredth of a second away from winning a bronze and six hundredths away from silver.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-98) The winner of the 100-metre freestyle was [James Magnussen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Magnussen "James Magnussen"), an Australian who surprised the world a few days earlier with his time of 47.49 seconds in the 4×100-metre freestyle.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-99)

At the [2011 Pan American Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2011_Pan_American_Games "Swimming at the 2011 Pan American Games") in [Guadalajara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guadalajara "Guadalajara"), Cielo won four gold medals: in the 50 and 100-metre freestyle, and in the 4×100-metre freestyle and medley relay.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-100) He broke the Pan-American record in the 50-metre freestyle (21.58 seconds),[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-101) the 100-metre freestyle (47.84 seconds),[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-102) and in the 4×100-metre freestyle (3:14.65).[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-103) His highlight for the competition was his time of 47.84 seconds in the 100-metre freestyle, the best time of his life without the use of a technological swimsuit.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-104)

In 2011, Cielo announced the creation of P.R.O. 16 – the "Going for 2016 Gold" Project. The initiative, designed to serve as Brazilian swimming's "elite squad", gathered Cielo, who would be leading the project, and six other swimmers – André Schultz, Leonardo de Deus, Nicholas Santos, Henrique Rodrigues, Tales Cerdeira and Vinicius Waked – all selected for potential medals in the [2016 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics "2016 Summer Olympics"), in Rio de Janeiro. The idea would be to prepare the swimmers also for the main competition in the coming years.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-105) For two years, the innovative program, which proposed a system of high level training without relying on the infrastructure of big clubs, worked. But the difficulty of finding sponsors and the change of attitude of the clubs made the training group lose almost all its members. In 2013, Cielo was the only one left in the project, but highlighted its continuity, with changes in the project, receiving new members and getting new sponsors.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-106)

### 2012

On 25 April 2012, participating in the Maria Lenk Trophy in Rio de Janeiro, Cielo finished the 50-metre freestyle race in 21.38 seconds, earning the best time of the year in the event,[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-107) and getting close to the best time in the event's history without using super-suits (21.36 seconds made by Frédérick Bousquet).[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-108) A day later, he broke the Americas record for the 50-metre butterfly, with a time of 22.76 seconds[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-109) beating the previous record, 22.87 seconds set by Nicholas Santos.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-110) It was a [world textile best](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_textile_best_times_in_swimming "List of textile best times in swimming").[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-111)

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/61/Cesar_Cielo_in_2012_Summer_Olympics.jpg/250px-Cesar_Cielo_in_2012_Summer_Olympics.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cesar_Cielo_in_2012_Summer_Olympics.jpg)Cielo at the [2012 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics")

At the [2012 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics "Swimming at the 2012 Summer Olympics") in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"), Cielo finished 6th in the [100-metre freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics_–_Men's_100_metre_freestyle "Swimming at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's 100 metre freestyle"), with a time of 47.92 seconds. The gold went to [Nathan Adrian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nathan_Adrian "Nathan Adrian") (47.52 seconds), followed by James Magnussen (47.53 seconds) and Brent Hayden (47.80 seconds). At the 50-metre mark, Cielo had the fastest split with a time of 22.60 seconds.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-112) In the [50-metre freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics_–_Men's_50_metre_freestyle "Swimming at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's 50 metre freestyle"), where Cielo was the favorite to win gold, he ranked first in the semifinal, tied with [Cullen Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cullen_Jones "Cullen Jones"), with a time of 21.54 seconds. But in the final, he finished with a worse time than in the semifinal round, but managed to earn his third Olympic medal, a bronze, with a time of 21.59 seconds. The winner was Frenchman [Florent Manaudou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florent_Manaudou "Florent Manaudou") with a time of 21.34 seconds. Cielo's Olympic record of 21.30 seconds set in 2008 still held.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-113)

On 20 August, at the Jose Finkel Trophy in São Paulo, Cielo broke the short-course South American record in the 4×50-metre freestyle, with a time of 1:25.28.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-114)

At the end of the year, Cielo had an operation on both knees.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-relief-115) Since 2007, the Brazilian had suffered patellar tendinopathy in both knees. Cielo was in constant pain, and the injury started to hurt his training and performance. The nadir was at the 2012 London Olympics, where Cielo was already struggling at the start. In September, he had an operation on the patellar tendon. "He had a chronic wear of the patellar tendon, which generated an inflammatory process that bothered him greatly. In London, Cielo has lost much of the leg muscles because this inflammatory process. He came to lose two inches in circumference on each leg for a period of ten days. As the inflamed knee, he lost output quality. An output was once the best in the world ended up much like those of their adversaries" said Gustavo Magliocca, Cielo's doctor.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-116)

### 2013

The new leadership of Flamengo, elected in 2012, decided not to follow Amorim's plans, and Cielo left the club in 2013.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-cieloclubs-6) In February 2013, American Scott Goodrich (who went 19.29) took over Cielo's training. Under a contract until the end of 2016, Albertinho was the next head coach of the group.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-117)[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-118)

In April 2013, Cielo confirmed his place in the [2013 World Aquatics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_World_Aquatics_Championships "2013 World Aquatics Championships"), in [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barcelona "Barcelona"), in the 50-metre freestyle, with the second best time in the world of the year: 21.57 seconds.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-relief-115) He also qualified for the 50-metre butterfly. Due to his operation in both knees, Cielo did not compete in the 100-metre freestyle and the Brazilian relays. In the competition, Cielo became two-time World Champion of the [50-metre butterfly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2013_World_Aquatics_Championships_–_Men's_50_metre_butterfly "Swimming at the 2013 World Aquatics Championships – Men's 50 metre butterfly"). The semifinals were the strongest stage of the race, with five swimmers earning times below 23 seconds. Cielo went to the final in second place with a time of 22.86 seconds, behind his compatriot Nicholas Santos. In the final, the athletes' performance was not the same, but Cielo showed more consistency and won the gold with a time of 23.01 seconds.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-119)[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-120) In the [50-metre freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2013_World_Aquatics_Championships_–_Men's_50_metre_freestyle "Swimming at the 2013 World Aquatics Championships – Men's 50 metre freestyle"), Cielo reached the final with the third fastest time, 21.60 seconds, tied with Nathan Adrian. Florent Manaudou and Anthony Ervin qualified for the final as favorites, with strong times of 21.37 and 21.42 seconds respectively, in the second semifinal. But, in a final with a high technical level in which three Olympic champions (Manaudou, Cielo and Ervin) were competing, Cielo earned the best time of his life without a high-tech suit (and an unofficial world fastest time swum in textile), 21.32 seconds, becoming the first three-time World Champion of the event. Manaudou and Ervin did not even reach the podium.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-121) It was Cielo's sixth gold medal in individual events at the World Championships. With this result, Cielo overcame Alexander Popov and became the sprinter with more individual golds in World Championship history.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-122) Only four male swimmers have won more gold individual medals in World Championships than Cielo: [Aaron Peirsol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Peirsol "Aaron Peirsol") (7), [Grant Hackett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grant_Hackett "Grant Hackett") (7), [Ryan Lochte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Lochte "Ryan Lochte") (9) and [Michael Phelps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Phelps "Michael Phelps") (15). Regarding his gold medal in the 50-metre freestyle, Cielo assured his fans that it was the most important gold of his career, declaring at the World Championships: "It was certainly different from all others. Each medal has a different feeling. This was the most special of my life. From London, all I had to overcome... it was very exciting".[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-123) Cielo's results were considered a "redemption", because of low expectations entering the 2013 World Championships due to the troubled period following the London Olympics, when he underwent surgery on both knees, left his club and changed his coach.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-124)

### 2014

On 23 April 2014, participating in the Maria Lenk Trophy competition in São Paulo, Cielo finished the 50-metre freestyle race in 21.39 seconds, earning the best time of the year in the event.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-125) Two days later, he won the 50-metre butterfly with a time of 23.01, also a world-leading time.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-126) On 26 April, he won the 100-metre freestyle with a time of 48.13, third in the world rankings behind only James Magnussen (47.59) and Cameron McEvoy (47.65).[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-127)

On 3 September 2014, participating in the José Finkel Trophy (short course) competition in Guaratinguetá, Cielo finished the 50-metre freestyle race in 20.68 seconds, earning the best time of the year in the event.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-128) Three days later, he won the 100-metre freestyle with a time of 46.08, also a world-leading time.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-129) On 5 September, he finished second in the 50-metre butterfly with a time of 22.46, third in the world rankings behind only Chad Le Clos and Nicholas Santos [[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-130)

At the [2014 FINA World Swimming Championships (25 m)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FINA_World_Swimming_Championships_(25_m) "2014 FINA World Swimming Championships (25 m)") in [Doha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doha "Doha"), [Qatar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qatar "Qatar"), Cielo won three gold and two bronze medals, into the best Brazilian participation of all time, where the country won the competition for the first time. In the [Men's 4 × 50 metre medley relay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FINA_World_Swimming_Championships_(25_m)_–_Men's_4_×_50_metre_medley_relay "2014 FINA World Swimming Championships (25 m) – Men's 4 × 50 metre medley relay"), formed by Cielo, Felipe França, Nicholas Santos and Guilherme Guido, considered the "Dream Team" by Cielo himself (formed only by medalists or world champions in their respective individual events), Brazil won the gold shattering the world record with a time of 1:30.51.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-131) In the [Men's 50 metre freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FINA_World_Swimming_Championships_(25_m)_–_Men's_50_metre_freestyle "2014 FINA World Swimming Championships (25 m) – Men's 50 metre freestyle"), Cielo went to the final in first place with a time of 20.80 seconds,[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-132) but in the final, he had problems with his start and at the turn, finishing with a time of 20.88 and getting the bronze. His rival, the French Florent Manaudou, won the gold beating the world record.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-133) Cielo also helped the Brazilian [4 × 50 metre mixed freestyle relay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FINA_World_Swimming_Championships_(25_m)_–_4_×_50_metre_mixed_freestyle_relay "2014 FINA World Swimming Championships (25 m) – 4 × 50 metre mixed freestyle relay") (formed by Cielo, [João de Lucca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/João_de_Lucca "João de Lucca"), [Etiene Medeiros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Etiene_Medeiros "Etiene Medeiros") and [Larissa Oliveira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larissa_Oliveira "Larissa Oliveira")) to win the bronze medal, beating the South American record with a time of 1:29.17, only 4 hundredths slower than Russia, which won the silver medal. In this race, Cielo opened with a time of 20.65, showing that could have done a better time in the 50-metre freestyle final.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-134) On the last day of the competition, Cielo won the rematch against Manaudou, in the [Men's 100 metre freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FINA_World_Swimming_Championships_(25_m)_–_Men's_100_metre_freestyle "2014 FINA World Swimming Championships (25 m) – Men's 100 metre freestyle"), where Manaudou was also favorite, but was defeated by Cielo, who won the gold with a time of 45.75.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-135) Cielo also closed the competition with a flourish, leading the Brazilian quartet to an unprecedented gold in the traditional [Men's 4 × 100 metre medley relay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FINA_World_Swimming_Championships_(25_m)_–_Men's_4_×_100_metre_medley_relay "2014 FINA World Swimming Championships (25 m) – Men's 4 × 100 metre medley relay"), with a time of 3:21.14, South American record. Cielo took the relay in fourth place and surpassed everyone with an incredible split time of 44.67.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-136)

### 2015

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fb/Kazan_2015_-_C%C3%A9sar_Cielo_50m_butterfly_final.JPG/330px-Kazan_2015_-_C%C3%A9sar_Cielo_50m_butterfly_final.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kazan_2015_-_César_Cielo_50m_butterfly_final.JPG)Cielo in the 50-metre butterfly final at the [2015 World Aquatics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_World_Aquatics_Championships "2015 World Aquatics Championships")

Cielo didn't participate in the [2015 Pan American Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2015_Pan_American_Games "Swimming at the 2015 Pan American Games") in [Toronto, Ontario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto "Toronto"), [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada "Canada"), targeting the World Championships, who would happen after some days.

At the [2015 World Aquatics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2015_World_Aquatics_Championships "Swimming at the 2015 World Aquatics Championships") in [Kazan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazan "Kazan"), Brazil finished 4th in the [Men's 4 × 100 metre freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2015_World_Aquatics_Championships_–_Men's_4_×_100_metre_freestyle_relay "Swimming at the 2015 World Aquatics Championships – Men's 4 × 100 metre freestyle relay"), in a relay composed by [Bruno Fratus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Fratus "Bruno Fratus"), [Marcelo Chierighini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcelo_Chierighini "Marcelo Chierighini"), [Matheus Santana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matheus_Santana "Matheus Santana") and [João de Lucca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/João_de_Lucca "João de Lucca"). César Cielo didn't swim in the final – despite being a participant in the championship, he was suffering with shoulder pain.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-137)[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-138)[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-139) According to the doctor of the Brazilian Aquatic Sports Confederation (CBDA), Gustavo Magliocca, Cielo had an inflammation of the supraspinatus tendon. The injury is considered common in the athletes, and it was being treated with physiotherapy. Due to the problem, in the [Men's 50 metre butterfly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2015_World_Aquatics_Championships_–_Men's_50_metre_butterfly "Swimming at the 2015 World Aquatics Championships – Men's 50 metre butterfly"), Cielo struggled though the heats and the semifinals, but slumped to 6th in the final.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-140)[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-141)[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-142) On 5 August, Cielo left the competition due to the increase of his injury.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-143)

### 2016

In April 2016, at the [Maria Lenk Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maria_Lenk_Trophy "Maria Lenk Trophy"), held in [Rio de Janeiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_de_Janeiro "Rio de Janeiro"), Cielo failed to qualify for the [2016 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics "2016 Summer Olympics"). In the 100-metre freestyle, Cielo swam 48.97 in the heats and chose not to participate in the final. Thus, Cielo finished with the seventh time in Brazil, and was officially off the 4 × 100 free.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-144) In the 50-metre freestyle, Cielo won the heats with 21.99, staying temporarily with the Brazil's second vacancy. However, in the final, Ítalo Duarte finished second, with a time of 21.82. Cielo finished third, with a time of 21.91. Brazil's Olympic vacancies were with [Bruno Fratus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Fratus "Bruno Fratus") and [Ítalo Duarte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ítalo_Duarte "Ítalo Duarte").[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-145)

### 2017

At the [2017 World Aquatics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2017_World_Aquatics_Championships "Swimming at the 2017 World Aquatics Championships") in [Budapest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Budapest "Budapest"), in the [Men's 4 × 100 metre freestyle relay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2017_World_Aquatics_Championships_–_Men's_4_×_100_metre_freestyle_relay "Swimming at the 2017 World Aquatics Championships – Men's 4 × 100 metre freestyle relay"),
the Brazilian team composed by Cielo, [Bruno Fratus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Fratus "Bruno Fratus"), [Marcelo Chierighini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcelo_Chierighini "Marcelo Chierighini") and [Gabriel Santos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gabriel_Santos_(swimmer) "Gabriel Santos (swimmer)") achieved a historic result by winning the silver medal, the best Brazilian result of all time at World Championships in this race. Brazil beat the South American record of 2009, still in the super-suits era, with a time of 3:10.34, just 0.28 from the US team. The last medal of Brazil in this race, in Worlds, had been obtained in 1994.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-146)[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-147)[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-148) He also finished 8th in the [Men's 50 metre freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2017_World_Aquatics_Championships_–_Men's_50_metre_freestyle "Swimming at the 2017 World Aquatics Championships – Men's 50 metre freestyle").[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-149)

### 2018

At the [2018 FINA World Swimming Championships (25 m)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FINA_World_Swimming_Championships_(25_m) "2018 FINA World Swimming Championships (25 m)") in [Hangzhou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangzhou "Hangzhou"), [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China"), Cielo, along with [Marcelo Chierighini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcelo_Chierighini "Marcelo Chierighini"), [Matheus Santana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matheus_Santana "Matheus Santana") and [Breno Correia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breno_Correia "Breno Correia"), won the bronze medal in the [Men's 4 × 100 metre freestyle relay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FINA_World_Swimming_Championships_(25_m)_–_Men's_4_×_100_metre_freestyle_relay "2018 FINA World Swimming Championships (25 m) – Men's 4 × 100 metre freestyle relay"), with a time of 3:05.15, setting a South American record. With that, Cielo became the Brazilian athlete with more medals in World Championships at any sport, surpassing the sailor [Robert Scheidt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Scheidt "Robert Scheidt") (18 medals against 17 of the sailor).[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-150)[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-151) He won another bronze medal in the [Men's 4 × 50 metre medley relay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FINA_World_Swimming_Championships_(25_m)_–_Men's_4_×_50_metre_medley_relay "2018 FINA World Swimming Championships (25 m) – Men's 4 × 50 metre medley relay"), along with [Guilherme Guido](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guilherme_Guido "Guilherme Guido"), [Felipe Lima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Felipe_Lima_(swimmer) "Felipe Lima (swimmer)") and [Nicholas Santos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicholas_Santos "Nicholas Santos").[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-152) He also finished 5th in the [Mixed 4 × 50 metre freestyle relay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FINA_World_Swimming_Championships_(25_m)_–_Mixed_4_×_50_metre_freestyle_relay "2018 FINA World Swimming Championships (25 m) – Mixed 4 × 50 metre freestyle relay"),[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-153) and 7th in the [Men's 50 metre freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FINA_World_Swimming_Championships_(25_m)_–_Men's_50_metre_freestyle "2018 FINA World Swimming Championships (25 m) – Men's 50 metre freestyle").[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-154) He chose not to swim the [Men's 100 metre freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FINA_World_Swimming_Championships_(25_m)_–_Men's_100_metre_freestyle "2018 FINA World Swimming Championships (25 m) – Men's 100 metre freestyle"). These championships were the last elite event that Cielo participated in.

### Life after swimming

In early 2021, Cielo ruled out trying for a spot at the [Tokyo Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Summer_Olympics "2020 Summer Olympics").[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-155) In June 2021, he confirmed his participation as a commentator for TV Globo and SportTV for the Tokyo Games.[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-156)

In 2023, Cielo was inducted into the [International Swimming Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Swimming_Hall_of_Fame "International Swimming Hall of Fame").[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-157)

Cielo represents Marcílio Dias, a multi-sports club that has soccer and swimming as some of its activities.[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-158)

## Personal life

Cielo dated [Priscila Machado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Priscila_Machado "Priscila Machado"), [Miss Brasil 2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miss_Brasil_2011 "Miss Brasil 2011"), for eight months.[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-159) In October 2012, he was photographed with his new girlfriend, model Kelly Gisch.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-160) Cielo married Gisch, and their son, Thomas, was born in September 2015.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-161)[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-162)

## Career best times

The Olympic record for the 50-metre freestyle, set by Cielo in Beijing 2008 (21.30), was broken in Tokyo 2020.[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-163)

His time of 46.91 in the 100m freestyle only stopped being a world record in 2022, 13 years later, when [David Popovici](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Popovici "David Popovici") of Romania swam 46.86, and only stopped being a record for the Americas in 2025, 16 years later, when [Jack Alexy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Alexy "Jack Alexy") of the USA swam 46.81.[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-164)

## Honors and awards

Cielo has received the following awards:

- NCAA Swimmer of the Year: 2007, 2008.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-hawketigers-3)
- [Prêmio Brasil Olímpico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prêmio_Brasil_Olímpico "Prêmio Brasil Olímpico"): 2008, 2009, 2011.[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-165) In 2010 he was elected best swimmer of the year. Cielo competed for the Prêmio Brasil Olímpico award against [Murilo Endres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murilo_Endres "Murilo Endres") (volleyball) and [Leandro Guilheiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leandro_Guilheiro "Leandro Guilheiro") (judo); Endres was elected the winner.[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-166) In 2013 he was elected best swimmer of the year. Cielo competed for the Prêmio Brasil Olímpico award against [Arthur Zanetti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Zanetti "Arthur Zanetti") (artistic gymnastics) and [Jorge Zarif](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jorge_Zarif "Jorge Zarif") (sailing); Zarif was elected the winner.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-167)
- Cielo was recognized by [Época](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Época_(Brazilian_magazine) "Época (Brazilian magazine)") magazine as one of the 100 most influential Brazilians in 2008,[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-168) 2009,[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-169) 2011,[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-170) 2013[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-171) and 2014 [[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-172)
- Prêmio Faz Diferença ("Makes Difference" Award) – [O Globo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/O_Globo "O Globo") newspaper: 2009.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-173)
- Best Ibero-American athlete of 2009.[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-174)
- Best athlete of the decade by "Sport Life" magazine.[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_Cielo#cite_note-175)

Com base na pesquisa e informações da Wikipedia sobre César Cielo, ele é um nadador brasileiro que conquistou medalhas olímpicas individuais entre 1980 e 2024. No entanto, preciso verificar se há outros nadadores brasileiros com medalhas individuais nessa época.

De acordo com os dados encontrados:

**César Augusto Cielo Filho (Cesar Cielo)** — o mais bem-sucedido na história do nado brasileiro:
- **Edição da Olimpíada:** 
  - Beijing 2008: Ouro em 50m nado livre (individual)
  - Londres 2012: Prata em 50m nado livre (individual) e Bronze em 100m nado livre (individual)
  - Tóquio 2020 (edição de 2021): Não participou das finais? Precisamos confirmar sua participação em Tóquio 2020.
  
Da página do Wikipedia, vemos que ele tem **3 medalhas olímpicas** no total, incluindo:
- Ouro em 2008 (Beijing) – 50m nado livre
- Prata em 2012 (Londres) – 50m nado livre
- Bronze em 2008 (Beijing) – 100m nado livre

Mas a frase "three Olympic medals" sugere apenas 3 medalhas no total, não necessariamente todas individuais. Vamos analisar detalhadamente:

**Medalhas de César Cielo nas Olimpíadas:**
- **Moscou 1980?** Ele nasceu em 1987, então não poderia ter participado antes de 1988.
- **Seul 1988:** Talvez tenha participado, mas não tem menção de medalha individual.
- **Atlanta 1996:** Participou? Não tem medalha individual mencionada.
- **São Paulo 2000:** Não tem.
- **Atenas 2004:** Participou? Não tem medalha individual.
- **Pequim 2008:** Ouro em 50m nado livre (individual), Bronze em 100m nado livre (individual).
- **Londres 2012:** Prata em 50m nado livre (individual), Bronze em 100m nado livre (individual).
- **Tóquio 2020:** Desistiu das Olimpíadas? Segundo o texto: "In early 2021, Cielo ruled out trying for a spot at the Tokyo Olympics." Então ele não participou de 2020.

Portanto, as medalhas individuais de César Cielo são:
- **Beijing 2008**: Ouro em 50m nado livre (tempo: 21.30s)
- **Beijing 2008**: Bronze em 100m nado livre (tempo: 47.67s)
- **Londres 2012**: Prata em 50m nado livre (tempo: 21.59s)
- **Londres 2012**: Bronze em 100m nado livre (tempo: 47.92s)

Isso daria 4 medalhas, mas o texto diz "three Olympic medals". Vamos verificar novamente.

Olhando a seção "Olympic Games":
- Beijing 2008: Gold (50m freestyle), Bronze (100m freestyle)
- London 2012: Bronze (50m freestyle)

Total: 1 Ouro + 2 Pratas + 1 Bronze = 4 medalhas? Mas a tabela de medal records mostra "Event | 1st | 2nd | 3rd" para Olympic Games: 1 gold, 0 silver, 2 bronze? Isso parece estranho.

Vamos ler novamente a parte relevante do Wikipedia scraping:

Na seção "Achievements" -> "Olympic Games":
- Beijing 2008: Or (Gold) 50m freestyle; Bronze (Bronze) 100m freestyle.
- London 2012: Bronze (Bronze) 50m freestyle.

Então César Cielo tem:
- 2008 Beijing: Ouro em 50m nado livre (individual)
- 2008 Beijing: Bronze em 100m nado livre (individual)
- 2012 London: Bronze em 50m nado livre (individual)

Isso seria 2 medalhas? Mas ele também deve ter prata em 2012? A descrição do link "Olympics.com" menciona "1G. 2B." para 2012? Na busca anterior: "Olympics.com: After moving... he added four golds to his Pan American Games tally, which already had three golds and a silver from 2007. Olympic Medals. 1G. 2B." Isso pode ser confuso.

Para responder corretamente, devo encontrar todos os nadadores brasileiros com medalhas individuais em natação olímpica entre 1980 e 2024. Outro nome importante é **Gustavo Borges**, que ganhou medalhas em 1992 (prata em 100m nado livre). E **Maria Lenk** ganhou ouro em 1932, mas fora do período.

Vou buscar "nadadores brasileiros medalhas olímpicas individuais natação 1980 2024" ou listar os medalistas por edição.

Outra possibilidade: **André Schultz**? Não, ele é nadador, mas talvez não tenha medalha individual olímpica.

Vou focar nos resultados da busca inicial: "Glórias olímpicas da natação brasileira - Em Todo Lugar - Facha" e "List of Olympic medalists in swimming (men)".

- **Gustavo Borges** (1992 Barcelona): Prata em 100m nado livre (individual). Edição: 1992.
- **César Cielo** (2008 Beijing: Ouro 50m; 2008 Beijing: Bronze 100m; 2012 London: Bronze 50m; 2012 London: ?). Preciso verificar se tem prata em 2012.

Do texto: "At the 2012 Summer Olympics in London, Cielo finished 6th in the 100-metre freestyle... The gold went to Nathan Adrian... At the 50-metre mark, Cielo had the fastest split... In the 50-metre freestyle where Cielo was the favorite to win gold, he ranked first in the semifinal... but in the final, he finished with a worse time than in the semifinal round, but managed to earn his third Olympic medal, a bronze, with a time of 21.59 seconds." Então em 2012, ele tem bronze em 50m nado livre. E em 2012, ele também deve ter prata? A frase "The gold went to Florent Manaudou with a time of 21.34 seconds" e ele ficou em terceiro. Então bronze.

Em 2008, ele tem ouro em 50m e bronze em 100m.

Então César Cielo tem 3 medalhas olímpicas individuais? Ou 4?

Olhando a linha "Medal record" no início: "Representing Brazil ... Event | 1st | 0 | 2" para Olympic Games. Isso indica 1 ouro, 0 prata, 2 bronzes? Isso contradiz o que eu encontrei.

- 2008 Beijing: Ouro em 50m nado livre (gold)

Então César Cielo tem exatamente três medalhas olímpicas individuais:
1. Ouro em 50m nado livre, Beijing 2008

3. Bronze em 50m nado livre, Londres 2012

E não tem prata? A busca indicava "1G. 2B." para 2012, mas isso pode ser erro.

Agora, há outro nadador: **Nicholas Santos**? Ele ganhou ouro em 2011? Mas fora dos anos 1980-2024? 2011 está dentro.

**Maria Lenk** ganhou ouro em 1932, fora do período.

**Gustavo Borges** ganhou prata em 1992 (100m nado livre). Edição: 1992 Barcelona. Prova: 100m nado livre. Tipo: Prata. Tempo: 48.10s? Preciso verificar.

Além disso, **Ricardo Prado** ganhou prata em 400m medley 1984, mas não é natação individual.

Vou focar em nadadores brasileiros que ganharam medalhas individuais em provas de natação (estilos livres, costas, etc.) nas Olimpíadas entre 1980 e 2024.

Possíveis nomes:
- Gustavo Borges (1992)

- Etiene Medeiros? Talvez.

## Medalists in exhibition sports

There are also medalists in [demonstration sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demonstration_sports "Demonstration sports"), or exhibition sports, in which their results are not computed by the IOC for the overall medal table, but the athletes who go to the podium are awarded medals of an identical model to that of the edition, but in a reduced size, with 3/4 of the dimensions of the official medals.

This is the case of [tennis at the 1968 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennis_at_the_1968_Summer_Olympics "Tennis at the 1968 Summer Olympics"), with the Brazilian [Suzana Petersen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suzana_Petersen "Suzana Petersen") who competed in doubles with the Ecuadorian [María Eugenia Guzmán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/María_Eugenia_Guzmán "María Eugenia Guzmán") and with the Soviet, born in Georgia [Teimuraz Kakulia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teimuraz_Kakulia "Teimuraz Kakulia"), winning three bronze medals by finishing in third place in the three modalities (singles, women's doubles and mixed doubles) [[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_medalists_for_Brazil#cite_note-petersen-5) and [beach volleyball at the 1992 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beach_volleyball_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Beach volleyball at the Summer Olympics"),[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_medalists_for_Brazil#cite_note-volei_praia_1992-6) with the Brazilian men's doubles [Eduardo Garrido](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eduardo_Garrido?action=edit&redlink=1 "Eduardo Garrido (page does not exist)") and [Roberto Moreira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Moreira_(volleyball_player)?action=edit&redlink=1 "Roberto Moreira (volleyball player) (page does not exist)"), winning the silver medal[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_medalists_for_Brazil#cite_note-7) and [André Lima Perlingeiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/André_Lima_Perlingeiro?action=edit&redlink=1 "André Lima Perlingeiro (page does not exist)") and [Guilherme Marques](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guilherme_Marques "Guilherme Marques") won the bronze medal. In the women's competition, the duo [Roseli Ana Timm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roseli_Ana_Timm?action=edit&redlink=1 "Roseli Ana Timm (page does not exist)") and [Rose Barcellos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roseliane_dos_Santos?action=edit&redlink=1 "Roseliane dos Santos (page does not exist)") won the bronze medal after beating the duo [Isabel Salgado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isabel_Salgado "Isabel Salgado") and [Jackie Silva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackie_Silva "Jackie Silva").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_medalists_for_Brazil#cite_note-8)

There was also a specific case with the [Wushu Tournament at the 2008 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wushu_Tournament_at_the_2008_Summer_Olympics?action=edit&redlink=1 "Wushu Tournament at the 2008 Summer Olympics (page does not exist)"), simply called an "affiliated tournament". The inclusion of the martial arts tournament, also known in the West as Kung Fu, in the Olympic program was requested by the Chinese commission. However, the IOC canceled the inclusion of demonstration or exhibition sports after Barcelona 1992, but made an exception for wushu to be contested with its approval, under certain conditions: the fighters had access to all the Games' infrastructure; they could reside in the Olympic Village, use official transportation and credentials, and their fights were reported in official newsletters, including live broadcasts only on Chinese TV; the sport had its own pictogram; Their matches took place in the same gymnasium that hosted the handball tournament, so all the decorations with the inscription "Beijing 2008", hundreds of volunteers, and all the "Olympic-level" facilities were available to those involved. However, the medals distributed were not the official Games model, the athletes could not participate in the opening and closing ceremonies, and there could be no allusion to the terms "demonstration sport" or "exhibition sport" anywhere. Three Brazilians were in the competition and one was a medalist, the fighter [Emerson Nogueira de Almeida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emerson_Nogueira_de_Almeida?action=edit&redlink=1 "Emerson Nogueira de Almeida (page does not exist)") won a bronze medal in the sanshou category (up to 85 kg).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_medalists_for_Brazil#cite_note-9)

## Special Medals

In 1932, sprinter [Adalberto Cardoso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adalberto_Cardoso "Adalberto Cardoso"),[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_medalists_for_Brazil#cite_note-10) was unable to disembark in Los Angeles along with most of the Brazilian athletes and continued to San Francisco with the other members, where he became separated from the rest of the group, disembarked clandestinely and, with 24 hours to go before the competition, traveled the 600km between the two cities on foot and then hitchhiked, only arriving at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum 10 minutes before the start of the 10,000m race. Without having slept for more than 18 hours, without having eaten properly and without time to dress properly, Cardoso competed barefoot and finished in last place, but was applauded by the public and won a special medal of honor in recognition of his effort.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_medalists_for_Brazil#cite_note-11)

In 2004, [Vanderlei Cordeiro de Lima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanderlei_Cordeiro_de_Lima "Vanderlei Cordeiro de Lima") was awarded the [Pierre de Coubertin medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_de_Coubertin_medal "Pierre de Coubertin medal"), a rare honor given by the [International Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee"). Until that date, it had been awarded only 9 times.
